observations: body L1-L4: the sign of right ascension is printed as one character, an A whose right stroke is the stem of an R; it is set so (the left half of the A joined to the R). Each formula is centred where it is printed; the bars after «60°» (L3-L4, 10.2 and 9.7 pt) are minus signs. Specks over «medii» (L1), in the left margin of L2, to the right of the fraction of L2 and under the bar of L3 are not transcribed; the d of «ascendentis» in the numerator of L4 is broken.

body L1-L4: with s the semidiurnal arc of the ascendant, the formulas put the cusps XI and XII s/3 and 2s/3 of right ascension after the midheaven, II and III one and two thirds of the seminocturnal arc 180° − s after the ascendant: (180° − s)/3 = 60° − s/3. These are al-Battānī's rules of p. 73-74: s/3 is the temporal hour of the ascendant doubled, 60° − s/3 its «residuum» (p. 74, L9-L10, cited in note 3).

body L6-L17: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the circle (radius 64.7 pt) and its six diameters to the points 7 and a, 8 and 2, 9 and 3, 10 and 4, 11 and 5, 12 and 6 of the equator, drawn as twelve radii from the point where they meet (0.2 pt from the centre of the circle; each pair is straight within 0.8°); outside the circle the figures of the equator, inside the numerals of the houses, bold italic. I, II, III, IV and VIII stand on rising lines and are set turned through 8° to 16°. A blot (3.5 by 2.6 pt) below X and a speck to the left of IV are not drawn.

body L6-L17: as drawn, the houses XII, XI and X take 40.7°, 41.0° and 41.7° of the equator (together 123.5°, the semidiurnal arc from a to 10), IX, VIII and VII 17.9°, 19.2° and 20.0° (57.1°); opposite, VI, V and IV take 40.3°, 41.1° and 41.7°, III, II and I 18.4°, 18.9° and 19.0°. A larger and a smaller house make 60° (note 3). The arcs are those of an illustration: at ar-Raqqah (latitude 36°, obliquity 23° 35′) the semidiurnal arc of a point of the ecliptic is at most 108° 29′.
body L8, L11: a speck after «502» (L8) and one after «Le» (L11) are not transcribed.

body L12-L14: the apostrophes of «l’horizon» (L12, L14) and «quoiqu’il» (L13) are printed as wedges leaning down to the right, like the grave accent of «à» (L16); the others as raised commas. All are set as apostrophes.
body L18, L20, L25: «peut–être», «60–61», «al–Battānī» and «az–Zar-» have long dashes (5.4 to 5.6 pt; those of «peut–être» and «60–61» touch the letters beside them).
body L22-L26: the accent of «lámina» (L23) is the acute, as in «ángulos» (L24) and in note 3; the d of «redondo» (L22) and the t of «Ptholomeo» (L26) are broken.
body L30: the dash after «a)» measures 9.6 pt; the hyphen of «27-30» 3.4 pt.

body L31-L33: a heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which goes on to p. 250. It concerns p. 75, L27-L30, where the true motion of the Moon is less than the mean from 0° to 95° and from 265° to 360° of the anomaly, and «Soli quoque idem contingit». The bar before the second «maxima» (L32, 10.1 pt) is a minus sign. Al-Battānī's own tables (Part II, p. 81) give the greatest equation of the Moon, 5° 1′ 0″, at 95°, and that of the Sun, 1° 59′ 10″, at 92°: 90° + 1° 59′ 10″ = 91° 59′ 10″ and 270° − 1° 59′ 10″ = 268° 0′ 50″, Schiaparelli's 92° and 268°.

notes_left L1-L6: the end of Schiaparelli's note 3 of p. 248. The semidiurnal arc of the nadir of a point is the seminocturnal arc of the point, so the two arcs make 180°, and a larger and a smaller house (a third of each) 60°. «p. 74, l. 9-10» is al-Battānī's «Eadem tempora duplicata de 60° deme».
notes_left L6: the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 8.9 pt, the hyphen of «9-10» 3.1 pt; the second A of the name prints without its bar, and its full stop stands high.
notes_right L1: the Greek name is printed «Οὐαλῆς», with the circumflex on the η (the usual form is Οὐάλης); the closing parenthesis of «(2)» is broken.
notes_right L6-L7: the X and the closing parenthesis of «LX)» (L6) are broken; the hyphen of «209-210» (L7) measures 2.8 pt.
